correctness.rationale: The one-sweep XOR law follows from independent edge switches, with the special collision at the highest differing bit. Conditioned on difference, first-card position is uniform. Counting maximal one bits yields a d-state Markov kernel K=(I+(n-1)1 pi^T)/n with eigenvalues 1,1/n. Invariance of uniform pairs gives the power identity. Independence of the reduced d rows proves exact rank and zero multiplicity. TV follows by counting the positive deviations on exactly n/2^j XOR strings. All quantifiers d>=1,m>=1, endpoint j are checked; exact rational exhaustive endpoint checks for d<=5 plus actual two-step compositions d<=3 passed 39668 assertions. These finite checks are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a standard shuffle where one marked card is already exactly uniform after one coordinate sweep, the exact two-card profile quantifies the first genuinely relational obstruction and its sudden n-fold contraction on the next sweep. A dimension-uniform rank-one tagged-pair reduction and exact spectral multiplicities distinguish two-label relaxation from full-deck relaxation; the precise worst-start finite-size result is a natural stochastic-process invariant, not an arbitrary small instance or routine numerical improvement.
